gloss_line.label: HIGHEST GLOSS, as actually drawn on the plate
gloss_line.note: Not a radial through the origin. Drifts from 8.9:1 at the left end to 7.8:1 at the right, so ratio alone does not fully describe it.

source: Stull, R.T. (1912). Influences of Variable Silica and Alumina on Porcelain Glazes of Constant RO. Trans. Am. Ceram. Soc. XIV. Polygons digitized from the printed Stull Diagram plate.
warning: Regions are cone 11 only. They do not shift when another cone is selected. Known limitation - the chart annotates it rather than hiding it.

regions.label: Unfused
regions.provenance: digitized from the printed Stull Diagram label positions
regions.note: Too much alumina for the flux to dissolve. Stiff, dry, opaque.

regions.label: Matte
regions.provenance: digitized from the printed Stull Diagram label positions
regions.note: Excess alumina relative to silica leaves the surface un-glassy.

regions.label: Semi-matte
regions.provenance: digitized from the printed Stull Diagram label positions
regions.note: Transitional. Stull's own boundary here is a curve, not a straight line.

regions.label: Bright gloss
regions.provenance: digitized from the printed Stull Diagram label positions
regions.note: Stull's bright glossy zone. The printed HIGHEST GLOSS line runs through it.

regions.label: Under-fired
regions.provenance: digitized from the printed Stull Diagram label positions
regions.note: Silica high relative to alumina, but not enough heatwork to melt it smooth.

regions.label: Crazing risk
regions.provenance: alumina ceiling read off the plate at the CRAZED label; silica ceiling INFERRED, not measured - least certain number here
regions.note: Overlay, not an exclusive region: it sits on top of whatever band is underneath. Crazing depends on the clay body as much as on the glaze, so no chart can guarantee it.
